sentences: In the building control process, the start is Do Building Regulations apply to the work; if no, no notification required, and if yes, has the work commenced.

In the building control process, if the work has commenced, apply to the local authority; if not, the work may be checked by the local authority or an approved inspector or carried out by a competent person.
In the building control process, after applying to the local authority the next step is local authority building control under the Building Regulations 2010.

In the building control process, where the work may be checked by the local authority or an approved inspector or carried out by a competent person, the next question is whether all the building work is covered by a competent person scheme or a third-party scheme for certification.

In the building control process, if all the building work is covered by a competent person scheme or a third-party scheme for certification, there is no need to submit a notice to the local authority, and the competent person or the scheme operator will notify the local authority of the work and provide them and the building occupier with a certificate of completion within 30 days of completion of the work; if not, the work may be checked by the local authority or an approved inspector, and work covered by a competent person scheme or a third-party scheme for certification can take place at the same time.
In the building control process, work checked by the local authority or an approved inspector goes either by the local authority route or the approved inspector route.
In the building control process, the local authority route is local authority building control under the Building Regulations 2010, which asks whether the work involves any of the listed cases.

In the building control process, if the work involves erecting or working on a building where the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 applies or will apply after the work is complete, erecting a building that fronts a private street, or erecting a building over a sewer, the applicant must deposit a full plans application; if not, the applicant may deposit a building notice application, and additional plans and details may be requested by the local authority.

In the building control process, after a full plans application the local authority must provide a substantive assessment of the plans and details and must approve or reject plans within five weeks or two months (with agreement), and must consult with the fire authority and, where appropriate, the sewerage undertaker and consider their views.
In the building control process, after a building notice application work may start after the local authority has had at least two clear working days’ notice.

In the building control process, work may start after the local authority has had at least two clear working days’ notice, and if the full plans application or submitted details under a building notice have not been assessed and approved, the work will be deemed ‘at risk’.

In the building control process, the local authority will provide an inspection framework and must be notified at these certain stages in order for inspection to take place, and where the local authority is satisfied that work complies with the Building Regulations, it will issue a completion certificate.

In the building control process, the approved inspector route is approved inspectors under the Building (Approved Inspectors etc.) Regulations 2010, and in conjunction with the approved inspector an initial notice must be given to the local authority.

In the building control process, if the initial notice is accepted by the local authority, request plan assessment and plans certificate, if desired, and where applicable the plans certificate is issued to both client and local authority; if not, provide additional information, amend notice or submit application to local authority.
In the building control process, the next step on the approved inspector route is to agree a site inspection plan with the approved inspector.

In the building control process, the approved inspector must consult the fire authority and, where appropriate, the sewerage undertaker, taking due regard of their views, and the plans certificate or final certificate cannot be issued until 15 working days have elapsed.

In the building control process, where the approved inspector is satisfied that work complies with the Building Regulations, it will issue a final certificate to both the applicant and the local authority within eight weeks of completion (note 1).

In the building control process, note 1 says the approved inspector must issue a final certificate within four weeks of occupation for buildings other than dwellings or eight weeks for dwellings, and Regulation 17(7) of the Approved Inspectors Regulations allows a local authority to extend these time periods either before or after expiry.

fixes.target: chapter-6-local-authority-building-control-and-approved-inspectors-table-1: Local authority building control and approved inspectors

columns: Local authority building control and approved inspectors
rows: Local authority route
Local authority building control under the Building Regulations 2010

Does the work involve any of the following: 1. Erecting or working on a building where the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 applies or will apply after the work is complete? 2. Erecting a building that fronts a private street? 3. Erecting a building over a sewer?
Yes: The applicant must deposit a full plans application
No: The applicant may deposit a building notice application – additional plans and details may be requested by the local authority

The local authority must provide a substantive assessment of the plans and details and must approve or reject plans within five weeks or two months (with agreement). The local authority must consult with the fire authority and, where appropriate, the sewerage undertaker and consider their views

Work may start after the local authority has had at least two clear working days’ notice. If the full plans application or submitted details under a building notice have not been assessed and approved, the work will be deemed ‘at risk’

The local authority will provide an inspection framework and must be notified at these certain stages in order for inspection to take place. Where the local authority is satisfied that work complies with the Building Regulations, it will issue a completion certificate
Approved inspector route
Approved inspectors under the Building (Approved Inspectors etc.) Regulations 2010
In conjunction with the approved inspector an initial notice must be given to the local authority
Is initial notice accepted by the local authority?
No: Provide additional information, amend notice or submit application to local authority
Yes: Request plan assessment and plans certificate, if desired. Where applicable, plans certificate is issued to both client and local authority
Agree site inspection plan with approved inspector

The approved inspector must consult the fire authority and, where appropriate, the sewerage undertaker, taking due regard of their views. The plans certificate or final certificate cannot be issued until 15 working days have elapsed

Where the approved inspector is satisfied that work complies with the Building Regulations, it will issue a final certificate to both the applicant and the local authority within eight weeks of completion1

NOTES: 1. The approved inspector must issue a final certificate within four weeks of occupation for buildings other than dwellings or eight weeks for dwellings. Regulation 17(7) of the Approved Inspectors Regulations allows a local authority to extend these time periods either before or after expiry.
